exact_missing_items: The rerun confirms that these were not just vague "help gaps", but concrete missing contracts:
The rerun did **not** overturn the prior conclusion that the major issue is incomplete ledger transfer rather than missing whole primitives.
The rerun makes it clear that the concern/action/governance tranche is missing not just "some schemas", but the following concrete families:
The result is that node-first routing and attempt-native runtime identity still cannot flow cleanly through Usage and Evidence without compatibility translation.
The routing and command-normalization model now depends on checks that `GATE-010` cannot express, which means the gate layer is behind the owner contract layer.

The runtime identity model across the rewrite now needs more than Persona/model/account disclosure. It also needs execution-role and operational-identity disclosure, and this owner doc has not caught up yet.
The system now has canonical field-name modernization without canonical scope modernization.
The tail still has broad, meaningful signal at the fifth model pass; it still merits carrying the full tranche into the final `GPT-5.3-Codex` pass rather than narrowing early.
Then the canonical-record section partially regresses again by keeping:
There are still unresolved architectural edges around DAE enforcement, OpenCode bridge limits, promoted-feature shell ownership, and runtime identity provenance.
